subject.title: Subagent sessions persist after completion, main session becomes unresponsive

question: Should completed run-mode subagent sessions remain visible history by default, be hidden/archived automatically, or be deleted after terminal delivery, and how should that interact with yielded-parent wake/resume behavior?
rationale: Current code intentionally preserves cleanup=keep run sessions and tests assert retained rows, but the issue reports that retained state makes status/session surfaces misleading and can coincide with parent-message delays; changing this is a user-visible session-history and runtime contract decision.

options.title: Preserve history, fix active projections
options.body: Keep completed child transcripts by default, but make session/task/Control UI/WebChat projections immediately mark them terminal and non-blocking, with explicit cleanup actions for pruning.

options.title: Auto-archive completed runs
options.body: Hide or archive completed one-shot subagent sessions after terminal cleanup by default, accepting a retention behavior change that needs docs and upgrade proof.

options.title: Delete completed run sessions
options.body: Remove one-shot child sessions after successful terminal delivery, maximizing cleanup but discarding default inspectable history unless users opt in elsewhere.

recommendation.title: Preserve history, fix active projections
recommendation.body: Keep completed child transcripts by default, but make session/task/Control UI/WebChat projections immediately mark them terminal and non-blocking, with explicit cleanup actions for pruning.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision spans core session retention, Gateway sessions.list, task cleanup, and product behavior where steipete has the strongest current-line and adjacent stale-task history signal.
